<div class="page-summary">
  <p>How selfdoc transforms Markdown templates into a static site: the build pipeline, directive resolution, theme system, and auxiliary outputs.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="architecture"><a class="heading-link" href="#architecture" aria-label="Link to section: Architecture">#</a>Architecture</h1>
<p>This page explains how selfdoc works at a high level -- what happens when you run <code>selfdoc build</code>, how directives get resolved, and how themes control the output. For internal implementation details (tokenizer internals, extractor protocol, resolver dispatch chain), see <a href="../internals/">Internals</a>.</p>
<h2 id="build-pipeline-overview"><a class="heading-link" href="#build-pipeline-overview" aria-label="Link to section: Build Pipeline Overview">#</a>Build Pipeline Overview</h2>
<p>The build transforms your <code>docs/</code> Markdown templates into a deployable static HTML site through 7 stages. Each stage receives the output of the previous one and produces a deterministic result:</p>
<ol><li><strong>Scan</strong> -- walk <code>docs/</code> for <code>.md</code> files, parse frontmatter</li><li><strong>Resolve directives</strong> -- replace directive markers with generated Markdown content (from source code or content transforms)</li><li><strong>Tokenize</strong> -- split the resolved Markdown into typed block tokens</li><li><strong>Render</strong> -- dispatch each token to a block-level HTML renderer</li><li><strong>Post-process</strong> -- apply heuristic transforms (code tabs, step guides, API entries, definitions, LCP promotion)</li><li><strong>Generate HTML</strong> -- wrap rendered content in a full page shell with navigation, metadata, and styles</li><li><strong>Auxiliary output</strong> -- generate sitemap, Atom feed, search index, OG images, <code>llms.txt</code>, and compressed companions</li></ol>
<p>There is no shared mutable state between stages, so each one can be tested and debugged independently.</p>
<h2 id="how-directives-resolve"><a class="heading-link" href="#how-directives-resolve" aria-label="Link to section: How Directives Resolve">#</a>How Directives Resolve</h2>
<p>When you write a directive like <code>:-: ref path=&quot;mypackage.core&quot;</code>, the build pipeline resolves it through a three-level dispatch chain. Each level is tried in order and resolution stops at the first match, so content directives take precedence over custom directives, which take precedence over the language extractor:</p>
<ol><li><strong>Content directives</strong> -- callouts (<code>callout-note</code>, <code>callout-warning</code>, etc.) and <code>list-glossary</code> are handled first. These transform body content into styled HTML without needing source code access.</li></ol>
<ol><li><strong>Custom directives</strong> -- if your <code>selfdoc.json</code> declares a <code>&quot;directives&quot;</code> map, the resolver loads the referenced Python script and calls its <code>resolve(attrs, config, body)</code> function.</li></ol>
<ol><li><strong>Language extractor</strong> -- the built-in extractor for your project's language handles the directive. This is the most common path for directives like <code>ref</code>, <code>table-schema</code>, and <code>code-test</code>.</li></ol>
<p>If nothing can resolve a directive, selfdoc emits an inline error marker (<code>&gt; *[selfdoc: ...]*</code>) in the rendered output so you can spot it immediately.</p>
<h3 id="what-each-directive-extracts"><a class="heading-link" href="#what-each-directive-extracts" aria-label="Link to section: What each directive extracts">#</a>What each directive extracts</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">What each directive extracts</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Directive</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">What it pulls from your code</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>ref</code></td><td role="gridcell">Module docstring, exported functions, classes with signatures and docs</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>table-schema</code></td><td role="gridcell">Dataclass/struct/interface fields as a Markdown table</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>code-test</code></td><td role="gridcell">Test function source code (whole file or a specific function)</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>code-help</code></td><td role="gridcell">CLI argument parser definitions and help text</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>table-config</code></td><td role="gridcell">Configuration keys with types and descriptions</td></tr>
</tbody>
<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<h2 id="how-themes-work"><a class="heading-link" href="#how-themes-work" aria-label="Link to section: How Themes Work">#</a>How Themes Work</h2>
<p>Themes control colors, typography, layout, and component styling through CSS custom properties. selfdoc ships with two built-in themes (<strong>minimal</strong> and <strong>clean</strong>), both including full dark mode, high contrast, reduced motion, and print support.</p>
<p>The theme system works in layers:</p>
<ul><li><strong>Theme CSS</strong> defines all custom properties in <code>:root</code> -- colors, fonts, spacing, shadows</li><li><strong>Dark mode</strong> uses a dual-selector strategy: <code>@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)</code> for automatic OS detection, plus <code>[data-theme=&quot;dark&quot;]</code> for manual toggle</li><li><strong>Custom overrides</strong> via <code>docs/custom.css</code> are injected after the theme, so your rules always win</li><li><strong>High contrast</strong> responds to <code>prefers-contrast: more</code> with stronger borders and text</li></ul>
<p>See the <a href="../theming/">Theming</a> page for the full property reference and design tool.</p>
<h2 id="auxiliary-outputs"><a class="heading-link" href="#auxiliary-outputs" aria-label="Link to section: Auxiliary Outputs">#</a>Auxiliary Outputs</h2>
<p>After the main HTML pipeline completes, the build generates 6 categories of companion files that enhance search engine discoverability, social sharing, client-side search, AI access, and transfer performance. These are all written to the same output directory alongside the HTML pages:</p>
<ul><li><strong>Sitemap</strong> (<code>sitemap.xml</code>) -- standard sitemap with page URLs and last-modified dates</li><li><strong>Atom feed</strong> (<code>feed.xml</code>) -- for RSS readers, respects per-page <code>feed: false</code> frontmatter</li><li><strong>Search index</strong> (<code>pagefind/</code>) -- the Pagefind index and search UI, built from the finished HTML</li><li><strong>OG images</strong> -- OpenGraph card PNGs for social sharing</li><li>**<code>llms.txt</code>** -- structured plain-text index for LLM consumption, plus <code>llms-full.txt</code> with all content</li><li><strong>Compressed companions</strong> -- gzip (and brotli if available) pre-compressed versions for efficient serving</li></ul>
<h2 id="post-processors"><a class="heading-link" href="#post-processors" aria-label="Link to section: Post-Processors">#</a>Post-Processors</h2>
<p>After block rendering produces HTML, 5 regex-based post-processors detect cross-block patterns and apply semantic enhancements. These operate on the joined HTML string rather than individual tokens, because the patterns they detect span multiple blocks:</p>
<ul><li><strong>Code tabs</strong> -- consecutive code blocks with different languages become a tabbed interface</li><li><strong>Step guides</strong> -- ordered lists after headings containing "step", "guide", or "tutorial" get a <code>class=&quot;steps&quot;</code> for special styling</li><li><strong>API entries</strong> -- sequences of h3/h4 + code block + description are wrapped in <code>&lt;div class=&quot;api-entry&quot;&gt;</code> cards</li><li><strong>Definition ids</strong> -- every author-declared definition site (a definition list, the <code>list-glossary</code> directive, or a hand-written <code>&lt;dfn&gt;</code>) gets a <code>term-&lt;slug&gt;</code> id so the glossary can link to it. A term is only ever declared; prose that reads like a definition declares nothing.</li><li><strong>LCP promotion</strong> -- the first image is promoted from <code>loading=&quot;lazy&quot;</code> to <code>fetchpriority=&quot;high&quot;</code> for faster Largest Contentful Paint</li></ul>
<h2 id="staleness-tracking"><a class="heading-link" href="#staleness-tracking" aria-label="Link to section: Staleness Tracking">#</a>Staleness Tracking</h2>
<p>The build computes content hashes for each page and persists them. The <code>check</code> command later uses these hashes to detect when page content has changed but its frontmatter description has not been updated -- catching stale SEO metadata before it goes live.</p>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - top <=100){active=headings[i];}}tocLinks.forEach(function(a){a.removeAttribute('aria-current');});if(active){active.link.setAttribute('aria-current','page');active.link.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest',behavior: 'smooth'});}ticking=false;}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(!ticking){requestAnimationFrame(update);ticking=true;}},{passive: true});update();})();(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.heading-link').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();var url=window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + link.getAttribute('href');history.replaceState(null,'',link.getAttribute('href'));navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function(){var toast=document.createElement('span');toast.className='copy-toast';toast.textContent='Link copied!';link.parentElement.style.position='relative';link.parentElement.appendChild(toast);setTimeout(function(){toast.remove();},2000);});});});})();(function(){var article=document.querySelector('article');if(!article)return;article.querySelectorAll('table.tm-table').forEach(function(table){var thead=table.querySelector('thead');if(!thead)return;var ths=thead.querySelectorAll('th.sortable');ths.forEach(function(th,colIdx){th.addEventListener('click',function(){var tbody=table.querySelector('tbody');if(!tbody)return;var rows=Array.prototype.slice.call(tbody.querySelectorAll('tr'));var asc=th.getAttribute('aria-sort')!=='ascending';ths.forEach(function(h){h.setAttribute('aria-sort','none');});th.setAttribute('aria-sort',asc ? 'ascending' : 'descending');var allNum=rows.every(function(r){var c=r.children[colIdx];if(!c)return false;var t=c.textContent.trim();return t !=='' && !isNaN(t);});rows.sort(function(a,b){var ac=a.children[colIdx],bc=b.children[colIdx];if(!ac || !bc)return 0;var at=ac.textContent.trim(),bt=bc.textContent.trim();if(allNum)return asc ? at - bt : bt - at;return asc ? at.localeCompare(bt): bt.localeCompare(at);});rows.forEach(function(r){tbody.appendChild(r);});});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>
</body>
</html>

<div class="page-summary">
  <p>Syntax highlighting, language icons, line numbers, run buttons, validated examples, annotations, diff highlighting, code tabs, and copy buttons in selfdoc.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="code-blocks"><a class="heading-link" href="#code-blocks" aria-label="Link to section: Code Blocks">#</a>Code Blocks</h1>
<p>Fenced code blocks in selfdoc get automatic syntax highlighting, language labels, and a copy button. Beyond the basics, you can enable line numbers, interactive run buttons, inline annotations, diff highlighting, and automatic language tabs.</p>
<h2 id="syntax-highlighting"><a class="heading-link" href="#syntax-highlighting" aria-label="Link to section: Syntax Highlighting">#</a>Syntax Highlighting</h2>
<p>selfdoc uses Pygments for build-time syntax highlighting, supporting hundreds of languages out of the box with no client-side JavaScript required. Highlighting happens during the build, so the output is static HTML with CSS classes. Just specify the language after the opening fence:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>def greet(name: str) -> str:     return f"Hello, {name}!"</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<p>Pygments supports hundreds of languages out of the box. If the language is not recognized, the code renders as plain text. Light and dark mode get separate Pygments styles (default/monokai) that switch automatically with the theme.</p>
<div class="tm-callout tm-callout-note" role="note">
<div class="tm-callout-title"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M17 3l4 4L8 20H4v-4z"/></svg>Note</div>
<div class="tm-callout-body"><p>Pygments is an optional dependency. If it is not installed, code blocks render without highlighting. Install it with <code>pip install pygments</code> or <code>uv add pygments</code>.</p></div>
</div>
<h2 id="language-icons"><a class="heading-link" href="#language-icons" aria-label="Link to section: Language Icons">#</a>Language Icons</h2>
<p>Each code block with a recognized language label gets a small SVG icon next to the language name in the header bar. The icons provide a visual cue that helps readers quickly identify the language, especially in tabbed code blocks showing the same concept in multiple languages. Control the icon style with <code>code_icons</code> in your config:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;code_icons&quot;: &quot;colorful&quot;
}</code></pre></figure>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">Language Icons</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Value</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>colorful</code> (default)</td><td role="gridcell">Full-color SVG icons for recognized languages</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>monochrome</code></td><td role="gridcell">Single-color icons that match the theme</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>none</code></td><td role="gridcell">No icons, just the language text label</td></tr>
</tbody>
<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<h2 id="line-numbers"><a class="heading-link" href="#line-numbers" aria-label="Link to section: Line Numbers">#</a>Line Numbers</h2>
<p>Enable line numbers globally or per block to help readers reference specific lines in discussions, reviews, or tutorials. Numbers are rendered via CSS counters in the gutter, so they do not get selected when a user copies code from the block. Enable globally with <code>line_numbers</code> in your config:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;line_numbers&quot;: true
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>Line numbers appear in the gutter via CSS counters, so they are not selectable when copying code. You can also enable line numbers per block using the <code>line_numbers</code> annotation in your fence:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>def example():     pass</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<p>Per-block annotations can also set the starting line number with <code>line_start</code>:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>    # This line is numbered 42     return result</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="run-buttons"><a class="heading-link" href="#run-buttons" aria-label="Link to section: Run Buttons">#</a>Run Buttons</h2>
<p>Enable interactive run buttons that let readers execute code examples in an online playground without leaving your documentation site. When enabled, each code block with a recognized language gets a "Run" button that opens the code in an appropriate external environment. Enable globally with <code>run_button</code> in your config:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;run_button&quot;: true
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>When enabled, code blocks get a "Run" button that opens the code in an appropriate online playground. You can also enable run buttons per block with the <code>run</code> annotation:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>print("Hello, world!")</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="validated-examples"><a class="heading-link" href="#validated-examples" aria-label="Link to section: Validated Examples">#</a>Validated Examples</h2>
<p>Mark a fenced block <code>validate</code> to declare it a complete, self-contained program, and <code>selfdoc check</code> will execute it against the validator you configure for that language. This catches the examples that parse cleanly but no longer work -- a renamed function, a changed signature, a removed keyword argument -- which syntax checking alone can never see. The marker is opt-in because most documentation snippets are deliberately partial:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>from mylib import greet</p>
<p>print(greet("world"))</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<p>Validators are declared per language in <code>selfdoc.json</code> under <code>examples</code>. Each value is a command template, and <code>{file}</code> is replaced with the path of the assembled snippet:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;examples&quot;: {
    &quot;python&quot;: &quot;uv run --directory python python {file}&quot;,
    &quot;go&quot;: &quot;scripts/validate-example-go.sh {file}&quot;
  }
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>Commands run from the project root, with a 60-second timeout. selfdoc writes the block's raw text to a scratch file whose extension names the language (<code>.py</code>, <code>.go</code>, <code>.ts</code>), passes the path in, and reports a non-zero exit as an <code>EXAMPLE002</code> error carrying the last five lines of the validator's output. A <code>validate</code> marker whose language has no configured command is an <code>EXAMPLE003</code> error -- never a silent skip, because a marker that validates nothing is indistinguishable from a passing one.</p>
<p>Blocks without the marker are untouched: they still get the <code>EXAMPLE001</code> syntax check and are never executed.</p>
<div class="tm-callout tm-callout-note" role="note">
<div class="tm-callout-title"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M17 3l4 4L8 20H4v-4z"/></svg>Note</div>
<div class="tm-callout-body"><p>There is no sandbox. Validators compile, type-check, and register -- they are not a harness for untrusted code, and the snippets they run are your own documentation.</p></div>
</div>
<h2 id="annotations"><a class="heading-link" href="#annotations" aria-label="Link to section: Annotations">#</a>Annotations</h2>
<p>Inline annotations turn numbered comments like <code>// [1]</code> or <code># [1]</code> into small clickable badges that reveal explanatory text on hover or focus. This lets you walk readers through code step by step without cluttering the source with long inline comments. Add annotation definitions after the closing fence:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>config = load_config()  # [1] result = build(config)  # [2]</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code>[1]: Reads selfdoc.json from the current directory
[2]: Resolves directives and writes HTML output</code></pre></figure>
<p>The numbered markers in the code become small badge elements. Click or focus a badge to see the annotation text. This is useful for walking through code step by step without cluttering the code itself with long comments.</p>
<h2 id="diff-highlighting"><a class="heading-link" href="#diff-highlighting" aria-label="Link to section: Diff Highlighting">#</a>Diff Highlighting</h2>
<p>Use the <code>diff</code> language identifier to get line-level add/remove coloring that visually distinguishes additions from deletions. selfdoc also auto-detects diff-style content in any code block where lines start with <code>+</code> or <code>-</code> characters. Use it to show migration steps or API changes:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>-old_function() +new_function(with_args=True)  unchanged_line()</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<p>Lines starting with <code>+</code> are highlighted green, lines starting with <code>-</code> are highlighted red, and lines starting with a space are neutral. selfdoc also auto-detects diff-style content in any code block where lines start with <code>+</code> or <code>-</code>.</p>
<h2 id="code-tabs"><a class="heading-link" href="#code-tabs" aria-label="Link to section: Code Tabs">#</a>Code Tabs</h2>
<p>When you place two or more fenced code blocks with different languages next to each other with no content between them, selfdoc automatically groups them into a tabbed interface. This is useful for showing the same concept in multiple languages, alternative installation methods, or platform-specific instructions. Only blocks with language labels participate in tab grouping:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label">`markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: `markdown"><code class="language-`markdown"></code></pre></figure>
<p>pip install selfdoc</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<p>npm install -g selfdoc</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code></code></pre></figure>
<p>This renders as a single code block with "python" and "bash" tabs. The user clicks a tab to see that version. Only blocks with language labels participate in tab grouping -- unlabeled blocks are left standalone.</p>
<div class="tm-callout tm-callout-tip" role="note">
<div class="tm-callout-title"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5"><path d="M4 12.5l5 5L20 6"/></svg>Tip</div>
<div class="tm-callout-body"><p>Code tabs are great for showing the same concept in multiple languages, or alternative installation methods. Put the most common option first.</p></div>
</div>
<h2 id="copy-button"><a class="heading-link" href="#copy-button" aria-label="Link to section: Copy Button">#</a>Copy Button</h2>
<p>Every code block gets a copy-to-clipboard button automatically. No config needed. It appears in the top-right corner of the block on hover and copies the raw code content (without line numbers or annotations).</p>
<p>Next: <a href="../custom-directives/">Custom Directives</a> --></p>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var COPY='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="12"/><path d="M4 16V4h12"/></svg>';var DONE='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5"><path d="M4 12.5l5 5L20 6"/></svg>';document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(figure){var code=figure.querySelector('pre code');var slot=figure.querySelector('.tm-code-actions');if(!code || !slot)return;var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='copy-btn';btn.type='button';btn.setAttribute('aria-label','Copy code');btn.innerHTML=COPY;btn.addEventListener('click',function(){navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.textContent).then(function(){btn.classList.add('copied');btn.innerHTML=DONE;setTimeout(function(){btn.classList.remove('copied');btn.innerHTML=COPY;},2000);});});slot.appendChild(btn);});})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - top <=100){active=headings[i];}}tocLinks.forEach(function(a){a.removeAttribute('aria-current');});if(active){active.link.setAttribute('aria-current','page');active.link.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest',behavior: 'smooth'});}ticking=false;}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(!ticking){requestAnimationFrame(update);ticking=true;}},{passive: true});update();})();(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.heading-link').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();var url=window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + link.getAttribute('href');history.replaceState(null,'',link.getAttribute('href'));navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function(){var toast=document.createElement('span');toast.className='copy-toast';toast.textContent='Link copied!';link.parentElement.style.position='relative';link.parentElement.appendChild(toast);setTimeout(function(){toast.remove();},2000);});});});})();(function(){var article=document.querySelector('article');if(!article)return;article.querySelectorAll('table.tm-table').forEach(function(table){var thead=table.querySelector('thead');if(!thead)return;var ths=thead.querySelectorAll('th.sortable');ths.forEach(function(th,colIdx){th.addEventListener('click',function(){var tbody=table.querySelector('tbody');if(!tbody)return;var rows=Array.prototype.slice.call(tbody.querySelectorAll('tr'));var asc=th.getAttribute('aria-sort')!=='ascending';ths.forEach(function(h){h.setAttribute('aria-sort','none');});th.setAttribute('aria-sort',asc ? 'ascending' : 'descending');var allNum=rows.every(function(r){var c=r.children[colIdx];if(!c)return false;var t=c.textContent.trim();return t !=='' && !isNaN(t);});rows.sort(function(a,b){var ac=a.children[colIdx],bc=b.children[colIdx];if(!ac || !bc)return 0;var at=ac.textContent.trim(),bt=bc.textContent.trim();if(allNum)return asc ? at - bt : bt - at;return asc ? at.localeCompare(bt): bt.localeCompare(at);});rows.forEach(function(r){tbody.appendChild(r);});});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>

<div class="page-summary">
  <p>How selfdoc compares to Sphinx, MkDocs, Docusaurus, VitePress, Rustdoc, Godoc, and TypeDoc -- features, tradeoffs, and where each tool shines.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="comparisons"><a class="heading-link" href="#comparisons" aria-label="Link to section: Comparisons">#</a>Comparisons</h1>
<p>selfdoc takes a different angle from most documentation generators: it extracts content directly from source code via 21 built-in directive types, supports 3 languages in a single tool, and produces a complete static site with search, SEO, and theming -- all from pure Python with 2 direct runtime dependencies and nothing to compile.</p>
<p>Here is how it stacks up against the popular alternatives.</p>
<h2 id="feature-comparison"><a class="heading-link" href="#feature-comparison" aria-label="Link to section: Feature Comparison">#</a>Feature Comparison</h2>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">Feature Comparison</caption>
<thead>

<h2 id="where-each-tool-shines"><a class="heading-link" href="#where-each-tool-shines" aria-label="Link to section: Where Each Tool Shines">#</a>Where Each Tool Shines</h2>
<h3 id="sphinx"><a class="heading-link" href="#sphinx" aria-label="Link to section: Sphinx">#</a>Sphinx</h3>
<p>The heavyweight champion for Python documentation. Sphinx has a massive ecosystem of extensions (intersphinx, autodoc, napoleon, etc.) and handles large, cross-referenced documentation sets better than anything else. If your project is Python-only, has hundreds of modules, and needs cross-project linking, Sphinx is the mature choice. The tradeoff is complexity: <code>conf.py</code> configuration, RST syntax by default, and a significant learning curve.</p>
<h3 id="mkdocs"><a class="heading-link" href="#mkdocs" aria-label="Link to section: MkDocs">#</a>MkDocs</h3>
<p>The simplest way to put Markdown docs online. MkDocs with Material theme gives you a polished site with minimal config. It does not extract from source code natively, but the ecosystem has plugins for most needs. If you are writing prose documentation (tutorials, guides, architecture docs) rather than API references, MkDocs is fast and well-supported.</p>
<h3 id="docusaurus"><a class="heading-link" href="#docusaurus" aria-label="Link to section: Docusaurus">#</a>Docusaurus</h3>
<p>React-powered documentation with MDX support. Docusaurus is the go-to for JavaScript/React projects that want interactive components in their docs. It has built-in versioning, i18n, and Algolia search integration. The cost is a full Node.js build chain and React in your docs pipeline.</p>
<h3 id="vitepress"><a class="heading-link" href="#vitepress" aria-label="Link to section: VitePress">#</a>VitePress</h3>
<p>Vue-powered and fast. VitePress is the spiritual successor to VuePress, optimized for speed and simplicity. Great for Vue ecosystem projects and sites that want a modern, minimal build. Less feature-rich than Docusaurus but lighter.</p>
<h3 id="rustdoc"><a class="heading-link" href="#rustdoc" aria-label="Link to section: Rustdoc">#</a>Rustdoc</h3>
<p>The gold standard for language-integrated documentation. Rustdoc extracts docs directly from Rust source comments, runs doctests, and hosts on docs.rs automatically. If you are documenting Rust, there is no reason to use anything else. The format is fixed -- you get what Rustdoc gives you.</p>
<h3 id="godoc"><a class="heading-link" href="#godoc" aria-label="Link to section: Godoc">#</a>Godoc</h3>
<p>Simple, convention-driven documentation for Go packages. Godoc reads package comments and produces consistent, browsable API docs hosted on pkg.go.dev. Like Rustdoc, it is purpose-built for one language and does that job well. No theming, no customization, no search -- just clean API references.</p>
<h3 id="typedoc"><a class="heading-link" href="#typedoc" aria-label="Link to section: TypeDoc">#</a>TypeDoc</h3>
<p>API documentation generator for TypeScript and JavaScript projects. TypeDoc reads JSDoc and TypeScript type information to produce reference docs. Strong on types and signatures, but focused on API references rather than full documentation sites.</p>
<h3 id="selfdoc"><a class="heading-link" href="#selfdoc" aria-label="Link to section: selfdoc">#</a>selfdoc</h3>
<p>selfdoc fits a niche that the others do not cover well: projects that want source-extracted documentation across Python, Go, and TypeScript without switching tools. The directive system keeps docs in sync with code automatically, and the built-in SEO, search, and deploy pipeline means fewer moving parts. The tradeoff is fewer themes and a smaller community than Sphinx or Docusaurus.</p>
<p>Next: <a href="../getting-started/">Getting Started</a> --></p>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - top <=100){active=headings[i];}}tocLinks.forEach(function(a){a.removeAttribute('aria-current');});if(active){active.link.setAttribute('aria-current','page');active.link.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest',behavior: 'smooth'});}ticking=false;}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(!ticking){requestAnimationFrame(update);ticking=true;}},{passive: true});update();})();(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.heading-link').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();var url=window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + link.getAttribute('href');history.replaceState(null,'',link.getAttribute('href'));navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function(){var toast=document.createElement('span');toast.className='copy-toast';toast.textContent='Link copied!';link.parentElement.style.position='relative';link.parentElement.appendChild(toast);setTimeout(function(){toast.remove();},2000);});});});})();(function(){var article=document.querySelector('article');if(!article)return;article.querySelectorAll('table.tm-table').forEach(function(table){var thead=table.querySelector('thead');if(!thead)return;var ths=thead.querySelectorAll('th.sortable');ths.forEach(function(th,colIdx){th.addEventListener('click',function(){var tbody=table.querySelector('tbody');if(!tbody)return;var rows=Array.prototype.slice.call(tbody.querySelectorAll('tr'));var asc=th.getAttribute('aria-sort')!=='ascending';ths.forEach(function(h){h.setAttribute('aria-sort','none');});th.setAttribute('aria-sort',asc ? 'ascending' : 'descending');var allNum=rows.every(function(r){var c=r.children[colIdx];if(!c)return false;var t=c.textContent.trim();return t !=='' && !isNaN(t);});rows.sort(function(a,b){var ac=a.children[colIdx],bc=b.children[colIdx];if(!ac || !bc)return 0;var at=ac.textContent.trim(),bt=bc.textContent.trim();if(allNum)return asc ? at - bt : bt - at;return asc ? at.localeCompare(bt): bt.localeCompare(at);});rows.forEach(function(r){tbody.appendChild(r);});});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>

<div class="page-summary">
  <p>Complete reference for selfdoc.json configuration options including project settings, themes, SEO, deployment, example validators, and branding.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="configuration"><a class="heading-link" href="#configuration" aria-label="Link to section: Configuration">#</a>Configuration</h1>
<p>selfdoc is configured via a <code>selfdoc.json</code> file in your project root. Run <code>selfdoc init</code> to generate a starter config interactively, or create one manually.</p>
<p><code>base_url</code> is the only required field. <code>source</code> is optional -- a codeless project (a portfolio or personal site that is nothing but Markdown pages) declares none, and directives that extract from source code are then a hard error rather than an empty section. Everything else is optional and has sensible defaults.</p>
<p>:<: callout-warning :=: ::: <code>base_url</code> is required for deployment. Without it, canonical URLs, sitemaps, OG tags, and Atom feeds will have broken links. Set it to the URL where your site will be hosted (e.g., <code>https://myproject.pages.dev</code>). :>:</p>
<h2 id="config-reference"><a class="heading-link" href="#config-reference" aria-label="Link to section: Config Reference">#</a>Config Reference</h2>
<p>The table below lists every field recognized by <code>selfdoc.json</code>, including the field type, whether it is required, and a description of what it controls. Required fields have no default and must be provided explicitly.</p>
<p>:-: config-schema</p>
<h2 id="common-configurations"><a class="heading-link" href="#common-configurations" aria-label="Link to section: Common Configurations">#</a>Common Configurations</h2>
<h3 id="minimal-python-project"><a class="heading-link" href="#minimal-python-project" aria-label="Link to section: Minimal Python project">#</a>Minimal Python project</h3>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;language&quot;: &quot;python&quot;,
  &quot;source&quot;: [&quot;src/&quot;],
  &quot;base_url&quot;: &quot;https://myproject.pages.dev&quot;
}</code></pre></figure>
<h3 id="go-project-with-deployment"><a class="heading-link" href="#go-project-with-deployment" aria-label="Link to section: Go project with deployment">#</a>Go project with deployment</h3>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;language&quot;: &quot;go&quot;,
  &quot;source&quot;: [&quot;pkg/&quot;, &quot;internal/&quot;],
  &quot;base_url&quot;: &quot;https://myproject.pages.dev&quot;,
  &quot;repo&quot;: &quot;https://github.com/user/myproject&quot;,
  &quot;branch&quot;: &quot;main&quot;,
  &quot;deploy&quot;: {
    &quot;provider&quot;: &quot;cloudflare-pages&quot;,
    &quot;project&quot;: &quot;myproject&quot;
  }
}</code></pre></figure>
<h3 id="full-featured-project-with-branding"><a class="heading-link" href="#full-featured-project-with-branding" aria-label="Link to section: Full-featured project with branding">#</a>Full-featured project with branding</h3>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;language&quot;: &quot;python&quot;,
  &quot;source&quot;: [&quot;mylib/&quot;],
  &quot;base_url&quot;: &quot;https://mylib.dev&quot;,
  &quot;docs&quot;: &quot;docs/&quot;,
  &quot;output&quot;: &quot;docs/_build/&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;A toolkit for building great things.&quot;,
  &quot;repo&quot;: &quot;https://github.com/user/mylib&quot;,
  &quot;branch&quot;: &quot;main&quot;,
  &quot;lang&quot;: &quot;en&quot;,
  &quot;theme&quot;: &quot;minimal&quot;,
  &quot;search&quot;: &quot;bar&quot;,
  &quot;search_engine&quot;: &quot;pagefind&quot;,
  &quot;min_coverage&quot;: 80,
  &quot;author&quot;: {
    &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Jane Doe&quot;,
    &quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://janedoe.example&quot;,
    &quot;same_as&quot;: [&quot;https://github.com/janedoe&quot;]
  },
  &quot;twitter&quot;: &quot;@janedoe&quot;,
  &quot;deploy&quot;: {
    &quot;provider&quot;: &quot;cloudflare-pages&quot;,
    &quot;project&quot;: &quot;mylib&quot;
  },
  &quot;branding&quot;: {
    &quot;tagline&quot;: &quot;Build great things.&quot;,
    &quot;cta_text&quot;: &quot;Get Started&quot;,
    &quot;cta_link&quot;: &quot;getting-started/&quot;,
    &quot;features&quot;: [
      {
        &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Fast&quot;,
        &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Blazing fast builds with zero dependencies.&quot;
      },
      {
        &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Flexible&quot;,
        &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Works with Python, Go, and TypeScript projects.&quot;
      }
    ]
  },
  &quot;directives&quot;: {
    &quot;changelog&quot;: &quot;scripts/changelog-directive.py&quot;
  }
}</code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="example-validators"><a class="heading-link" href="#example-validators" aria-label="Link to section: Example Validators">#</a>Example Validators</h2>
<p>The <code>examples</code> key maps a fenced-block language to the command that validates a snippet written in it. <code>selfdoc check</code> uses these commands for code blocks marked <code>validate</code> in their fence info string, writing each block to a scratch file and substituting its path for <code>{file}</code>:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;examples&quot;: {
    &quot;python&quot;: &quot;uv run --directory python python {file}&quot;,
    &quot;go&quot;: &quot;scripts/validate-example-go.sh {file}&quot;,
    &quot;ts&quot;: &quot;scripts/validate-example-ts.sh {file}&quot;
  }
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>Every command template must contain the <code>{file}</code> placeholder; a template without it is rejected when the config loads, since it would validate nothing. Keys are language names exactly as they appear after the opening fence, so a block opened with <code>```py</code> needs a <code>py</code> entry, not a <code>python</code> one. Omitting <code>examples</code> entirely turns the feature off, and any <code>validate</code> marker in the docs then reports <code>EXAMPLE003</code>. See the <a href="../check-guide/">Check Guide</a> for the full behavior.</p>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var COPY='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="12"/><path d="M4 16V4h12"/></svg>';var DONE='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5"><path d="M4 12.5l5 5L20 6"/></svg>';document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(figure){var code=figure.querySelector('pre code');var slot=figure.querySelector('.tm-code-actions');if(!code || !slot)return;var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='copy-btn';btn.type='button';btn.setAttribute('aria-label','Copy code');btn.innerHTML=COPY;btn.addEventListener('click',function(){navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.textContent).then(function(){btn.classList.add('copied');btn.innerHTML=DONE;setTimeout(function(){btn.classList.remove('copied');btn.innerHTML=COPY;},2000);});});slot.appendChild(btn);});})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - top <=100){active=headings[i];}}tocLinks.forEach(function(a){a.removeAttribute('aria-current');});if(active){active.link.setAttribute('aria-current','page');active.link.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest',behavior: 'smooth'});}ticking=false;}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(!ticking){requestAnimationFrame(update);ticking=true;}},{passive: true});update();})();(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.heading-link').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();var url=window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + link.getAttribute('href');history.replaceState(null,'',link.getAttribute('href'));navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function(){var toast=document.createElement('span');toast.className='copy-toast';toast.textContent='Link copied!';link.parentElement.style.position='relative';link.parentElement.appendChild(toast);setTimeout(function(){toast.remove();},2000);});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>

<article data-pagefind-body class="doc-body">
<span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-filter="version:0.38.1"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-filter="type:guide"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-filter="project:selfdoc"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-meta="project:selfdoc"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-meta="type:guide"></span>
<div class="content-header">
<nav class="tm-crumbs-nav" aria-label="Breadcrumb"><ol class="tm-crumbs"><li class="tm-crumb"><a class="tm-crumb-link" href="../index.html">Home</a></li><li class="tm-crumb"><span class="tm-crumb-current" aria-current="page">Directives Reference</span></li></ol></nav>

<details class="mobile-toc"><summary>On this page</summary><nav class="docs-toc" aria-label="On this page"><div class="docs-toc-head">Contents</div><a class="docs-toc-item" href="#syntax">Syntax</a>
<a class="docs-toc-item" href="#built-in-directives">Built-in Directives</a>
<a class="docs-toc-item sub" href="#the-exclude-attribute">The exclude Attribute</a>
<a class="docs-toc-item" href="#custom-directives">Custom Directives</a></nav></details>
<div class="page-summary">
  <p>Complete reference for all built-in selfdoc directives including code extraction, content blocks, and custom directive authoring.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="directives-reference"><a class="heading-link" href="#directives-reference" aria-label="Link to section: Directives Reference">#</a>Directives Reference</h1>
<p>selfdoc directives are inline blocks in Markdown templates that get resolved into content at build time. They pull live information from your source code, so documentation stays in sync with the implementation.</p>
<h2 id="syntax"><a class="heading-link" href="#syntax" aria-label="Link to section: Syntax">#</a>Syntax</h2>
<p>Directives use 6 marker types and come in two forms: self-closing one-liners for directives that need only attributes, and block directives for those that accept additional body content passed to the resolver function. The marker characters (<code>:-:</code>, <code>:&lt;:</code>, <code>:&gt;:</code>, <code>:=:</code>, <code>:::</code>, <code>:@:</code>) are designed to be visually distinctive in plain Markdown.</p>
<p>:<: callout-note :=: ::: Directives inside fenced code blocks (triple backticks) are ignored. You can safely show directive syntax in code examples without triggering resolution. :>:</p>
<p><strong>One-liner</strong> (self-closing, no body):</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: name key=&quot;value&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>Block</strong> (with body content):</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:&lt;: name key=&quot;value&quot;
::: body line 1
::: body line 2
:&gt;:</code></pre></figure>
<p>Block directives can also include additional attributes and a body separator:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:&lt;: name key=&quot;value&quot;
:@: another=&quot;attr&quot;
:=:
::: body content here
:&gt;:</code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="built-in-directives"><a class="heading-link" href="#built-in-directives" aria-label="Link to section: Built-in Directives">#</a>Built-in Directives</h2>
<p>The following table shows all built-in directives that selfdoc recognizes, their current implementation status (shipped or planned for a future release), and a brief description of what each directive extracts from source code or generates as content.</p>
<p>:-: catalog</p>
<h3 id="the-exclude-attribute"><a class="heading-link" href="#the-exclude-attribute" aria-label="Link to section: The exclude Attribute">#</a>The <code>exclude</code> Attribute</h3>
<p>The <code>table-schema</code> and <code>table-config</code> directives accept an optional <code>exclude</code> attribute — a comma-separated list of top-level keys to omit from the rendered table. Whitespace around commas is stripped. This is useful when a config or schema file contains keys that are too large, irrelevant, or internal to display in documentation, letting you render a focused subset of the file's structure.</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: table-config path=&quot;selfdoc.json&quot; exclude=&quot;versions, locales&quot;
:-: table-schema path=&quot;schema.json&quot; exclude=&quot;internal_field&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p>If any excluded key does not exist in the file, a hard error is produced (no silent skips). Works with JSON, TOML, and JSONC files. For <code>table-schema</code>, <code>exclude</code> only applies when the path points to a data file — it has no effect when extracting from a Python dataclass or Go struct.</p>
<h2 id="custom-directives"><a class="heading-link" href="#custom-directives" aria-label="Link to section: Custom Directives">#</a>Custom Directives</h2>
<p>You can extend selfdoc with project-specific custom directives by registering them in your <code>selfdoc.json</code> configuration file, pointing each directive name to a Python script that implements the resolution logic. Custom directives take priority over built-in directives of the same name:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;directives&quot;: {
    &quot;my-directive&quot;: &quot;scripts/my-directive.py&quot;
  }
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>Each custom directive script must export a <code>resolve(attrs, config, body)</code> function that returns a Markdown string:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M8 1C5.2 1 5.5 2.2 5.5 2.2V3.5H8v.5H3.5S1 3.7 1 6.5S3.2 9 3.2 9H4.5V7.7S4.4 5.5 6.7 5.5h2.5S11 5.5 11 3.8V2.3S11.3 1 8 1zM6.3 2a.6.6 0 110 1.2.6.6 0 010-1.2z" fill="#3776AB"/><path d="M8 15c2.8 0 2.5-1.2 2.5-1.2V12.5H8V12h4.5s2.5.3 2.5-2.5S12.8 7 12.8 7H11.5v1.3s.1 2.2-2.2 2.2H6.8S5 10.5 5 12.2v1.5S4.7 15 8 15zm1.7-1a.6.6 0 110-1.2.6.6 0 010 1.2z" fill="#FFD43B"/></svg> python</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: python"><code class="language-python">def resolve(attrs, config, body):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Called when :-: my-directive is encountered.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    return &quot;Generated content here&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<ul><li><code>attrs</code> — dict of key-value pairs from the directive line</li><li><code>config</code> — the full <code>selfdoc.json</code> configuration dict</li><li><code>body</code> — list of body lines (empty list for one-liners)</li></ul>
<p>Custom directives take priority over built-in directives of the same name.</p>
