<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var COPY='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="12"/><path d="M4 16V4h12"/></svg>';var DONE='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5"><path d="M4 12.5l5 5L20 6"/></svg>';document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(figure){var code=figure.querySelector('pre code');var slot=figure.querySelector('.tm-code-actions');if(!code || !slot)return;var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='copy-btn';btn.type='button';btn.setAttribute('aria-label','Copy code');btn.innerHTML=COPY;btn.addEventListener('click',function(){navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.textContent).then(function(){btn.classList.add('copied');btn.innerHTML=DONE;setTimeout(function(){btn.classList.remove('copied');btn.innerHTML=COPY;},2000);});});slot.appendChild(btn);});})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - top <=100){active=headings[i];}}tocLinks.forEach(function(a){a.removeAttribute('aria-current');});if(active){active.link.setAttribute('aria-current','page');active.link.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest',behavior: 'smooth'});}ticking=false;}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(!ticking){requestAnimationFrame(update);ticking=true;}},{passive: true});update();})();(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.heading-link').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();var url=window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + link.getAttribute('href');history.replaceState(null,'',link.getAttribute('href'));navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function(){var toast=document.createElement('span');toast.className='copy-toast';toast.textContent='Link copied!';link.parentElement.style.position='relative';link.parentElement.appendChild(toast);setTimeout(function(){toast.remove();},2000);});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>

<span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-filter="version:0.38.1"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-filter="type:glossary"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-filter="project:selfdoc"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-meta="project:selfdoc"></span><span class="pagefind-facet" data-pagefind-meta="type:glossary"></span>
<div class="content-header">
<nav class="tm-crumbs-nav" aria-label="Breadcrumb"><ol class="tm-crumbs"><li class="tm-crumb"><a class="tm-crumb-link" href="../index.html">Home</a></li><li class="tm-crumb"><span class="tm-crumb-current" aria-current="page">Glossary</span></li></ol></nav>

<div class="page-summary">
  <p>Alphabetical glossary of key terms used in the selfdoc documentation, including directives, extractors, frontmatter, themes, and build pipeline concepts.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="glossary"><a class="heading-link" href="#glossary" aria-label="Link to section: Glossary">#</a>Glossary</h1>
<p>This page defines 23 key terms used throughout the selfdoc documentation.</p>
<p>:<: list-glossary :=: ::: <strong>Directive</strong>: A marker in Markdown templates that selfdoc resolves into content at build time. Comes in one-liner (<code>:-:</code>) and block (<code>:&lt;: ... :&gt;:</code>) forms. ::: <strong>Extractor</strong>: A language-specific module that reads source code and extracts API information for directives. Selfdoc ships with extractors for Python, Go, and TypeScript. ::: <strong>Frontmatter</strong>: YAML-like metadata at the top of a Markdown file between <code>---</code> delimiters. Controls title, description, nav group, and other page settings. ::: <strong>Resolver</strong>: The dispatch layer that routes a parsed directive to the correct handler -- content directives, custom directives, or language extractors, in that order. ::: <strong>Tokenizer</strong>: A standalone module that splits Markdown into typed block tokens (headings, code blocks, tables, paragraphs, etc.) used by both the renderer and the lint system. ::: <strong>Theme</strong>: A set of CSS custom properties controlling colors, typography, layout, and component styling. Selfdoc ships with <code>minimal</code> and <code>clean</code> themes. ::: <strong>Callout</strong>: A content directive that renders a styled admonition box. Types include <code>callout-note</code>, <code>callout-warning</code>, <code>callout-tip</code>, <code>callout-danger</code>, and <code>callout-important</code>. ::: <strong>Code block</strong>: A fenced block of source code (triple backticks) that gets syntax-highlighted in the rendered output. Consecutive code blocks with different languages become tabbed. ::: <strong>OG card</strong>: An OpenGraph image generated for each page, used as the preview image when a link is shared on social media or messaging platforms. ::: <strong>Sitemap</strong>: An XML file (<code>sitemap.xml</code>) listing all page URLs and their last-modified dates, used by search engines for indexing. ::: <strong>Atom feed</strong>: An XML feed (<code>feed.xml</code>) that allows RSS readers to subscribe to documentation updates. Pages can opt out with <code>feed: false</code> in frontmatter. ::: <strong>Canonical URL</strong>: The definitive URL for a page, set via the <code>base_url</code> config field. Used in <code>&lt;link rel=&quot;canonical&quot;&gt;</code> tags and sitemaps to avoid duplicate content in search engines. ::: <strong>JSON-LD</strong>: Structured data embedded in each HTML page as a <code>&lt;script type=&quot;application/ld+json&quot;&gt;</code> block. Provides search engines with machine-readable metadata about the page. ::: <strong>Lint rule</strong>: An SEO or content quality check run by <code>selfdoc check</code>. Each rule has a code (e.g., SEO001) and produces warnings or errors with file locations. ::: <strong>Coverage</strong>: The percentage of public symbols in your source code that are referenced by at least one directive. Reported by <code>selfdoc check</code> and configurable via <code>min_coverage</code>. ::: <strong>Staleness</strong>: When a page's content has changed since the last build but its frontmatter description has not been updated. Detected by comparing content and description hashes. ::: <strong>Build pipeline</strong>: The seven-stage process that transforms Markdown templates into a static HTML site: scan, resolve, tokenize, render, post-process, generate HTML, auxiliary output. ::: <strong>Nav group</strong>: A frontmatter field (<code>nav_group</code>) that controls which section of the sidebar navigation a page appears in. Pages with the same nav group are grouped together. ::: <strong>Slug</strong>: The URL-friendly identifier derived from a page's filename. For example, <code>getting-started.md</code> becomes the slug <code>getting-started</code>, served at <code>/getting-started/</code>. ::: <strong>Search index</strong>: The Pagefind index under <code>pagefind/</code>, built from the finished HTML pages, powering the client-side full-text search in the rendered site. ::: <strong>Post-processor</strong>: A regex-based transform that runs after block rendering to detect cross-block patterns like consecutive code blocks (code tabs) or ordered lists after tutorial headings (step guides). ::: <strong>Custom directive</strong>: A project-specific directive defined in <code>selfdoc.json</code> that points to a Python script implementing <code>resolve(attrs, config, body)</code>. Takes priority over built-in directives. ::: <strong>Content directive</strong>: A directive that transforms body content into styled HTML without needing source code access. Includes callouts and <code>list-glossary</code>. :>:</p>

<footer class="page-footer"><div class="page-meta"><span><a class="edit-link" href="https://github.com/smm-h/selfdoc/edit/main/docs/glossary-terms.md" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edit this page on GitHub</a></span></div><nav class="page-nav"><a class="page-nav-prev" href="../code-blocks/"><span class="page-nav-label">Previous</span>&larr; Code Blocks</a><span class="page-progress">Page 7 of 9</span><a class="page-nav-next" href="../guides/getting-started/"><span class="page-nav-label">Next</span>Getting Started &rarr;</a></nav></footer>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>

  <p>Install selfdoc and generate your first documentation site in minutes. Covers installation, project setup, writing directives, and local development.</p>

<h1 id="getting-started"><a class="heading-link" href="#getting-started" aria-label="Link to section: Getting Started">#</a>Getting Started</h1>
<p>This guide walks you through installing selfdoc, setting up a project, writing your first directive, and previewing your documentation site locally.</p>
<h2 id="installation"><a class="heading-link" href="#installation" aria-label="Link to section: Installation">#</a>Installation</h2>
<p>selfdoc requires <strong>Python 3.11 or later</strong> and has 2 direct runtime dependencies: <code>strictcli</code> (its CLI framework) and <code>selfdoc-core</code> (the extraction engine), which between them add <code>strictspec</code> and <code>tomlkit</code>. All 4 are pure Python, so nothing compiles at install time and it works on Linux, macOS, and Windows with no platform-specific setup. Install it via pip from PyPI, or via npm as a thin Node wrapper around the Python package.</p>
<p>Install via pip:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">pip install selfdoc</code></pre></figure>
<p>Or via npm (a thin wrapper that delegates to <code>python3 -m selfdoc</code>):</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">npm install -g selfdoc</code></pre></figure>
<p>Verify the installation:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc --version</code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="initialize-a-project"><a class="heading-link" href="#initialize-a-project" aria-label="Link to section: Initialize a Project">#</a>Initialize a Project</h2>
<p>Navigate to the root of an existing codebase that you want to document. The <code>init</code> command detects your project language, creates the configuration file, and scaffolds a starter documentation template:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc init --base-url https://myproject.pages.dev</code></pre></figure>
<p><code>--base-url</code> is required: it is the address the site will be served from, selfdoc cannot infer it, and every canonical link, sitemap entry and feed URL is built from it.</p>
<p>This does three things:</p>
<ol><li><strong>Detects your project language</strong> from manifest files (<code>pyproject.toml</code> for Python, <code>go.mod</code> for Go, <code>tsconfig.json</code> or <code>package.json</code> for TypeScript/JavaScript).</li><li>**Creates <code>selfdoc.json</code>** -- the base URL you passed, source directories, docs path, output path, the version declaration and the <code>locales</code> array with a single entry. The emitted file builds as-is; nothing has to be added by hand. The version comes from your own manifest (<code>pyproject.toml</code>, <code>package.json</code> or <code>VERSION</code>); if your project has code but states no version there, <code>init</code> says so and stops rather than writing a number you never released.</li><li>**Creates <code>docs/index.md</code>** with a starter template that includes a <code>ref</code> directive pointing at your main module.</li></ol>
<p>A project with no detectable language is a <strong>codeless project</strong> -- a portfolio or personal site that is nothing but Markdown pages. <code>init</code> initializes it too: the config gets no <code>source</code> key, the starter page gets no <code>ref</code> directive, and instead of a <code>versions</code> array it gets <code>&quot;unversioned&quot;: true</code> -- the declaration that the project publishes no artifact and therefore has no public version. Its pages carry no version badge, no version search filter and no version picker. Directives that extract from source code are a hard error in such a project, so add a <code>source</code> entry before using one (and a <code>versions</code> array with it, since <code>unversioned</code> and <code>source</code> are mutually exclusive).</p>
<p>The <code>init</code> command also auto-commits the generated files unless you pass <code>--no-auto-commit</code>.</p>
<h2 id="project-structure"><a class="heading-link" href="#project-structure" aria-label="Link to section: Project Structure">#</a>Project Structure</h2>
<p>After initialization, your project will have a <code>selfdoc.json</code> configuration file at the project root and a <code>docs/</code> directory containing a starter Markdown template with a <code>ref</code> directive already pointing at your main module. Your existing source code is not modified:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code>your-project/
  selfdoc.json        # Configuration file
  docs/
    index.md          # Starter template
  src/ or lib/        # Your source code (unchanged)</code></pre></figure>
<h3 id="selfdocjson"><a class="heading-link" href="#selfdocjson" aria-label="Link to section: selfdoc.json">#</a>selfdoc.json</h3>
<p>The configuration file controls how selfdoc finds your source code, where to look for documentation templates, and where to write the generated HTML output. Only <code>language</code> and <code>source</code> are required -- everything else has sensible defaults that work for most projects:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;language&quot;: &quot;python&quot;,
  &quot;source&quot;: [&quot;mypackage/&quot;],
  &quot;docs&quot;: &quot;docs/&quot;,
  &quot;output&quot;: &quot;docs/_build/&quot;
}</code></pre></figure>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">selfdoc.json</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Field</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Required</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>language</code></td><td role="gridcell">yes</td><td role="gridcell">One of <code>python</code>, <code>go</code>, <code>typescript</code>, or <code>javascript</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>source</code></td><td role="gridcell">yes</td><td role="gridcell">List of directories containing source code to extract from</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>docs</code></td><td role="gridcell">no</td><td role="gridcell">Directory containing Markdown templates (default: <code>stricttools/docs/</code>)</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>output</code></td><td role="gridcell">no</td><td role="gridcell">Directory for generated HTML output (default: <code>stricttools/.docs-cache/build/</code>)</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>deploy</code></td><td role="gridcell">no</td><td role="gridcell">Deploy provider config -- see the deployment docs</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>directives</code></td><td role="gridcell">no</td><td role="gridcell">Map of custom directive names to script paths</td></tr>
</tbody>
<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<h3 id="the-docs-directory"><a class="heading-link" href="#the-docs-directory" aria-label="Link to section: The docs directory">#</a>The docs directory</h3>
<p>Every <code>.md</code> file in <code>docs/</code> is a documentation page that selfdoc will process during the build. Each file should start with YAML frontmatter containing at least a title and description for SEO metadata:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown"><span class="tm-code-line tm-code-del">--</span>
<span class="tm-code-line">title: API Reference</span>
<span class="tm-code-line">description: &quot;Complete API reference for mypackage.&quot;</span>
<span class="tm-code-line">order: 20</span>
<span class="tm-code-line tm-code-del">--</span>
<span class="tm-code-line"></span>
<span class="tm-code-line"># API Reference</span>
<span class="tm-code-line"></span>
<span class="tm-code-line">Your content here...</span></code></pre></figure>
<ul><li><code>title</code> -- used in the sidebar navigation and HTML <code>&lt;title&gt;</code></li><li><code>description</code> -- used in meta tags for SEO, and printed above the H1 on most pages</li><li><code>order</code> -- controls sidebar sort order (lower numbers appear first)</li></ul>
<h4 id="where-the-description-is-printed-on-the-page"><a class="heading-link" href="#where-the-description-is-printed-on-the-page" aria-label="Link to section: Where the description is printed on the page">#</a>Where the description is printed on the page</h4>
<p><code>description</code> always goes into the <code>&lt;meta name=&quot;description&quot;&gt;</code> tag. Whether it is <em>also</em> printed as a summary block above the H1 is decided by what the page is, never by what it says:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">Where the description is printed on the page</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Page</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Summary block above the H1</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>index.md</code> (the home page)</td><td role="gridcell">No -- the home page opens with its own lead paragraph</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell">A page declaring <code>type: post</code></td><td role="gridcell">No -- a post opens with its own lead paragraph</td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell">Every other page</td><td role="gridcell">Yes</td></tr>
</tbody>
<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<p>Printing it on a home page or a post says the same sentence twice inside one viewport. Everywhere else the block is a useful summary of what the page covers, so it stays. Nothing compares the description against the first paragraph: a layout that changed with the wording would be a layout nobody could predict.</p>
<p>Files are organized into a flat structure. The filename (minus <code>.md</code>) becomes the URL slug: <code>docs/api-reference.md</code> becomes <code>/api-reference/</code>.</p>
<h2 id="writing-your-first-directive"><a class="heading-link" href="#writing-your-first-directive" aria-label="Link to section: Writing Your First Directive">#</a>Writing Your First Directive</h2>
<p>Directives are the core feature of selfdoc -- inline markers in your Markdown templates that get replaced with content extracted from your source code at build time. They keep your documentation in sync with the implementation automatically.</p>
<p>Open <code>docs/index.md</code> (created by <code>selfdoc init</code>) and you will see something like:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown"><span class="tm-code-line tm-code-del">--</span>
<span class="tm-code-line">title: myproject</span>
<span class="tm-code-line">description: Documentation for myproject</span>
<span class="tm-code-line tm-code-del">--</span>
<span class="tm-code-line"></span>
<span class="tm-code-line"># myproject</span>
<span class="tm-code-line"></span>
<span class="tm-code-line">Welcome to the myproject documentation.</span>
<span class="tm-code-line"></span>
<span class="tm-code-line">## API Reference</span>
<span class="tm-code-line"></span>
<span class="tm-code-line">:-: ref path=&quot;myproject&quot;</span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The line <code>:-: ref path=&quot;myproject&quot;</code> is a self-closing directive. At build time, selfdoc will:</p>
<ol><li>Look up the <code>myproject</code> module in your source directories.</li><li>Extract its docstring, public functions, classes, and their signatures.</li><li>Replace the directive line with formatted Markdown content.</li></ol>
<h3 id="adding-more-directives"><a class="heading-link" href="#adding-more-directives" aria-label="Link to section: Adding more directives">#</a>Adding more directives</h3>
<p>selfdoc ships with 5 built-in directives for common documentation patterns, from extracting module-level API references to rendering configuration schemas as tables. Each directive uses a <code>path</code> attribute to identify the source file or module, and some accept additional attributes like <code>target</code> for specific symbols. Here are examples of each:</p>
<p><strong>Module reference</strong> -- extract docstrings and public API:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: ref path=&quot;mypackage.core&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>Schema table</strong> -- render a dataclass or config structure as a table:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: table-schema path=&quot;mypackage.config&quot; target=&quot;Settings&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>Test code</strong> -- embed a test function's source:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: code-test path=&quot;tests/test_core.py&quot; target=&quot;test_basic_usage&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>CLI help</strong> -- extract CLI usage and flags:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: code-help path=&quot;mypackage.cli&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>Config table</strong> -- render a JSON or TOML config file as a key-value table:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#333"/><text x="8" y="12.5" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">M</text></svg> markdown</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: markdown"><code class="language-markdown">:-: table-config path=&quot;selfdoc.json&quot;</code></pre></figure>
<p>Directives inside fenced code blocks (triple backticks) are ignored, so you can safely document directive syntax without triggering resolution.</p>
<h2 id="building"><a class="heading-link" href="#building" aria-label="Link to section: Building">#</a>Building</h2>
<p>Once you have written your Markdown templates with directive markers, generate the complete static HTML site with a single command. The build resolves all directives, converts Markdown to HTML, generates navigation and search indexes, and writes everything to the output directory:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc build</code></pre></figure>
<p>This resolves all directives in your <code>docs/</code> templates and writes HTML output to <code>docs/_build/</code> (or wherever <code>output</code> is configured in <code>selfdoc.json</code>).</p>
<p>The build output includes everything needed for a complete static site:</p>
<ul><li>HTML pages with sidebar navigation</li><li>Syntax-highlighted code blocks</li><li>Full-text search</li><li>Dark mode with system preference detection</li><li>XML sitemap and Atom feed</li><li>Structured data (JSON-LD) for search engines</li><li>Print stylesheet for PDF export</li></ul>
<p>After building, you will see a summary like:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code>Built 5 file(s) to docs/_build/</code></pre></figure>
<p>Any SEO warnings or directive errors are printed after the build summary. Errors cause a non-zero exit code; warnings are informational.</p>
<h2 id="local-development"><a class="heading-link" href="#local-development" aria-label="Link to section: Local Development">#</a>Local Development</h2>
<p>Preview your documentation site locally with automatic live reload powered by Server-Sent Events. The development server watches the output directory for file changes and pushes reload notifications to every connected browser tab, so your pages update instantly after each build without manual refreshing or browser extensions.</p>
<p>:<: callout-tip :=: ::: Run <code>selfdoc serve</code> alongside <code>selfdoc build</code> for a live preview workflow -- the browser reloads automatically via Server-Sent Events whenever the output changes. :>:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc serve</code></pre></figure>
<p>This starts a local HTTP server at <code>http://localhost:8000/</code> and watches the output directory for changes. When files change, connected browsers reload automatically via Server-Sent Events (SSE).</p>
<p>To use a different port:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc serve --port 3000</code></pre></figure>
<p>The typical development workflow is:</p>
<ol><li>Run <code>selfdoc serve</code> in one terminal.</li><li>Edit your Markdown templates in <code>docs/</code>.</li><li>Run <code>selfdoc build</code> in another terminal.</li><li>The browser reloads automatically with your changes.</li></ol>
<p>Press <code>Ctrl+C</code> to stop the server.</p>
<h2 id="checking-your-docs"><a class="heading-link" href="#checking-your-docs" aria-label="Link to section: Checking Your Docs">#</a>Checking Your Docs</h2>
<p>Validate that all directives resolve correctly, review documentation coverage against your public API surface, and catch SEO issues before publishing. The check command runs three categories of analysis and reports results with file locations and actionable diagnostic codes:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc check</code></pre></figure>
<p>This runs three checks:</p>
<ol><li><strong>Directive validation</strong> -- attempts to resolve every directive in your templates and reports any that fail (missing modules, invalid paths, etc.).</li><li><strong>Coverage analysis</strong> -- for Python projects, counts how many public symbols in your source are referenced by directives versus how many exist. For Go and TypeScript, coverage is reported based on exported symbols.</li><li><strong>SEO linting</strong> -- checks frontmatter, heading structure, meta descriptions, and other best practices.</li></ol>
<p>Example output:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"></span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code block"><code>Directive results:
  docs/index.md:12  ref path=&quot;mypackage&quot;        OK
  docs/api.md:8     ref path=&quot;mypackage.core&quot;    OK
  docs/api.md:20    table-schema path=&quot;...&quot;      OK

Coverage: 15/23 public symbols documented (65%)

SEO: 0 warnings, 0 errors</code></pre></figure>
<p>To suppress specific SEO warnings, pass <code>--ignore</code> with a comma-separated list of codes:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc check --ignore SEO007,SEO008</code></pre></figure>
<p>For machine-readable output (useful in CI):</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc check --json</code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="next-steps"><a class="heading-link" href="#next-steps" aria-label="Link to section: Next Steps">#</a>Next Steps</h2>
<p>Now that you have a working documentation site with live directives, full-text search, and dark mode, explore these topics to learn about advanced configuration, theming, deployment to production hosting, and the full directive reference:</p>
<ul><li><strong><a href="../directives/">Directives Reference</a></strong> -- complete reference for all built-in directives, block syntax, and custom directives.</li><li><strong><a href="../selfdoc-config/">Configuration</a></strong> -- all <code>selfdoc.json</code> options including deploy providers, coverage thresholds, and lint suppression.</li><li><strong><a href="../cli-index/">CLI Reference</a></strong> -- detailed documentation for every CLI command and flag.</li></ul>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var COPY='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="12"/><path d="M4 16V4h12"/></svg>';var DONE='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5"><path d="M4 12.5l5 5L20 6"/></svg>';document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(figure){var code=figure.querySelector('pre code');var slot=figure.querySelector('.tm-code-actions');if(!code || !slot)return;var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='copy-btn';btn.type='button';btn.setAttribute('aria-label','Copy code');btn.innerHTML=COPY;btn.addEventListener('click',function(){navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.textContent).then(function(){btn.classList.add('copied');btn.innerHTML=DONE;setTimeout(function(){btn.classList.remove('copied');btn.innerHTML=COPY;},2000);});});slot.appendChild(btn);});})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - 'ascending' : 'descending');var allNum=rows.every(function(r){var c=r.children[colIdx];if(!c)return false;var t=c.textContent.trim();return t !=='' && !isNaN(t);});rows.sort(function(a,b){var ac=a.children[colIdx],bc=b.children[colIdx];if(!ac || !bc)return 0;var at=ac.textContent.trim(),bt=bc.textContent.trim();if(allNum)return asc ? at - bt : bt - at;return asc ? at.localeCompare(bt): bt.localeCompare(at);});rows.forEach(function(r){tbody.appendChild(r);});});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>

<div class="page-summary">
  <p>Customize your selfdoc site with the three built-in themes, CSS custom properties, dark mode support, the build-time theme override that lets one theme be judged on real pages, and a visual design tool for iterating on styles.</p>
</div>
<h1 id="theming"><a class="heading-link" href="#theming" aria-label="Link to section: Theming">#</a>Theming</h1>
<p>selfdoc ships with three built-in themes and a comprehensive set of CSS custom properties that you can override without touching theme internals. Dark mode, high contrast, and print stylesheets work out of the box.</p>
<h2 id="choosing-a-theme"><a class="heading-link" href="#choosing-a-theme" aria-label="Link to section: Choosing a Theme">#</a>Choosing a Theme</h2>
<p>Set the <code>theme</code> field in your <code>selfdoc.json</code> configuration to select which built-in theme to use for your documentation site. The theme controls colors, typography, layout, and component styling. If omitted, the minimal theme is used by default:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#555"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{}</text></svg> json</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: json"><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;theme&quot;: &quot;minimal&quot;
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>Three themes are available:</p>
<ul><li><strong>minimal</strong> (default) -- GitHub-inspired styling with Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts. Blue accent color (<code>#0969da</code>), light sidebar background, dark topbar. Content-focused and familiar.</li><li><strong>clean</strong> -- Stripe-inspired styling with system fonts and a purple accent (<code>#5046e4</code>). White topbar, borderless code blocks, slightly taller line height (1.7 vs 1.6). Feels more polished and modern.</li><li><strong>tinymoon</strong> -- the <a href="https://github.com/smm-h/tinymoon">tinymoon</a> framework itself, not an imitation of it: dark by default, sharp corners everywhere, three vendored fonts (IBM Plex Sans for prose, IBM Plex Mono for anything that reads as data, Space Grotesk for headings), hairline borders with an accent glow instead of shadows, and a 100-180ms motion vocabulary. Blue accent (<code>#2d6cf4</code>). Tables, badges, breadcrumbs and metadata are all set in mono, and a faint grain overlay sits over the page.</li></ul>
<p>All three include full dark mode, high contrast, reduced motion, and print support.</p>
<h3 id="what-differs-about-tinymoon"><a class="heading-link" href="#what-differs-about-tinymoon" aria-label="Link to section: What differs about tinymoon">#</a>What differs about tinymoon</h3>
<p>Three things are worth knowing before choosing it.</p>
<p><strong>It is not a stylesheet in this repository.</strong> minimal and clean are single CSS files selfdoc owns. tinymoon is an <em>overlay</em> on the <a href="https://github.com/smm-h/tinymoon">tinymoon</a> framework, which selfdoc-core depends on: the stylesheet a page receives is the framework's own sheets -- <code>tokens</code>, <code>base</code>, <code>shell</code>, <code>primitives</code>, <code>widgets</code>, <code>prose</code>, in that order, byte for byte out of the installed package -- with selfdoc's overlay appended. The overlay carries the parts of a selfdoc page the framework has no shape for and a <em>bridge</em> that defines selfdoc's custom-property names as references to the framework's tokens. Upgrading the framework upgrades the theme.</p>
<p><strong>It rests in dark.</strong> The framework's <code>:root</code> is the dark palette and the light one is a reassignment, which is the reverse of the other two themes. A <code>custom.css</code> override still lands on the same custom property names, but a <code>:root</code> override will be changing the <em>dark</em> values. The light palette is in <code>html[data-theme=&quot;light&quot;]</code> for the explicit choice, and in <code>html:not([data-theme])</code> inside a <code>@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)</code> block for the system one -- so all three toggle states resolve in CSS alone, with no JavaScript involved in painting the right scheme.</p>
<p>**Its stylesheet is written into <code>css/</code> and ships files beside it.** The framework's <code>@font-face</code> rules address <code>../fonts/</code>, so the theme's stylesheet goes to <code>css/style.css</code> at the output root with the four woff2 faces in <code>fonts/</code>. Nothing is fetched from a font CDN and nothing is base64 in the stylesheet, so the faces are cached once for the whole site instead of re-downloaded with every sheet. In an assembled site the same payload is the site-level page chrome, under one content-hashed directory: a framework upgrade renames the directory, so no cache can serve the previous bytes against the new markup.</p>
<h2 id="previewing-a-theme"><a class="heading-link" href="#previewing-a-theme" aria-label="Link to section: Previewing a Theme">#</a>Previewing a Theme</h2>
<p>To see a theme on real pages without editing any project's configuration, pass <code>--theme</code> to a build:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#4EAA25"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">$_</text></svg> bash</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: bash"><code class="language-bash">selfdoc build --no-auto-commit --theme tinymoon</code></pre></figure>
<p>The override applies to that build only and is never written back to <code>selfdoc.json</code>. <code>selfdoc build</code> takes the same flag, and <code>selfdoc assembly preview --theme &lt;name&gt;</code> applies it to every checkout in an assembled preview at once -- which is the point: judging a theme means seeing the whole site under it, not one page. An unknown name is refused against the theme registry. With <code>--no-build</code>, where the override cannot reach the builds themselves, the preview checks that each checkout's existing build output really was produced under that theme -- an equality against the stylesheet a build writes, not a guess -- and hard-errors naming any checkout that was not.</p>
<h2 id="css-custom-properties"><a class="heading-link" href="#css-custom-properties" aria-label="Link to section: CSS Custom Properties">#</a>CSS Custom Properties</h2>
<p>Every visual aspect of a selfdoc site is controlled by CSS custom properties defined in <code>:root</code>. Override any of them in a <code>custom.css</code> file (see next section) to change colors, fonts, or spacing without forking the theme.</p>

<h3 id="layout-clean-only"><a class="heading-link" href="#layout-clean-only" aria-label="Link to section: Layout (clean only)">#</a>Layout (clean only)</h3>
<p>The clean theme defines two extra CSS custom properties not present in the minimal theme, controlling shadow depth and border radius for a more polished, card-like appearance. The minimal theme accesses these via CSS fallback syntax so they can still be overridden in <code>custom.css</code>:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">Layout (clean only)</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Property</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">clean default</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--shadow-md</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--radius</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>6px</code></td></tr>
</tbody>
<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<p>Minimal uses these via CSS fallbacks (e.g., <code>var(--radius, 4px)</code>) so they can still be overridden in custom.css for either theme.</p>
<h2 id="custom-styles"><a class="heading-link" href="#custom-styles" aria-label="Link to section: Custom Styles">#</a>Custom Styles</h2>
<p>Create a <code>docs/custom.css</code> file in your project to override any CSS custom property or add your own styling rules. selfdoc automatically detects this file during build and injects it after the theme stylesheet, so your rules take precedence over the built-in theme values.</p>
<p>Example -- change the accent color and body font:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#1572B6"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="7" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{;}</text></svg> css</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: css"><code class="language-css">:root {
    --link: #e63946;
    --link-hover: #c1121f;
    --sidebar-active: #e63946;
    --badge-bg: #e63946;
    --font-body: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif;
}</code></pre></figure>
<p>No build configuration is needed. Just save the file and run <code>selfdoc build</code>.</p>
<h2 id="dark-mode"><a class="heading-link" href="#dark-mode" aria-label="Link to section: Dark Mode">#</a>Dark Mode</h2>
<p>Both themes ship with a complete dark color palette that covers every CSS custom property, ensuring consistent contrast and readability across all page elements including code blocks, tables, and admonitions. Dark mode activates in two ways:</p>
<ol><li><strong>Automatic</strong> -- the <code>prefers-color-scheme: dark</code> media query matches the user's OS setting. This is the default behavior with no configuration needed.</li><li><strong>Manual toggle</strong> -- clicking the theme toggle button in the topbar sets <code>data-theme=&quot;dark&quot;</code> (or <code>&quot;light&quot;</code>) on the root element, overriding the OS preference.</li></ol>
<h3 id="how-the-selectors-work"><a class="heading-link" href="#how-the-selectors-work" aria-label="Link to section: How the selectors work">#</a>How the selectors work</h3>
<p>The theme CSS uses a layered selector strategy with two complementary rules that handle both automatic OS-preference detection via the <code>prefers-color-scheme</code> media query and explicit user toggle interactions via the <code>data-theme</code> attribute on the root element:</p>
<ul><li><code>@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme=&quot;light&quot;]) { ... } }</code> -- applies dark colors when the OS prefers dark, unless the user has explicitly toggled to light.</li><li><code>[data-theme=&quot;dark&quot;] { ... }</code> -- applies dark colors unconditionally when the toggle is set to dark, regardless of OS preference.</li></ul>
<h3 id="overriding-dark-mode-colors"><a class="heading-link" href="#overriding-dark-mode-colors" aria-label="Link to section: Overriding dark mode colors">#</a>Overriding dark mode colors</h3>
<p>To customize dark mode colors in your <code>custom.css</code> file, you must mirror the same dual-selector pattern used by the built-in themes so that your overrides apply in both automatic and manual dark mode:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#1572B6"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="7" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{;}</text></svg> css</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: css"><code class="language-css">/* Override dark mode accent */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    :root:not([data-theme=&quot;light&quot;]) {
        --link: #ff6b6b;
        --sidebar-active: #ff6b6b;
    }
}
[data-theme=&quot;dark&quot;] {
    --link: #ff6b6b;
    --sidebar-active: #ff6b6b;
}</code></pre></figure>
<h3 id="dark-mode-property-values"><a class="heading-link" href="#dark-mode-property-values" aria-label="Link to section: Dark mode property values">#</a>Dark mode property values</h3>
<p>The following table shows selected dark mode defaults for both the minimal and clean themes, useful as a reference when deciding which CSS custom properties to override in your <code>custom.css</code> dark mode rules:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">Dark mode property values</caption>
<thead>

<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--bg</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#0d1117</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#0a2540</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--text</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#c9d1d9</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#e3e8ee</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--heading</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#e6edf3</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#ffffff</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--link</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#58a6ff</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#9b93ff</code></td></tr>

<h2 id="high-contrast"><a class="heading-link" href="#high-contrast" aria-label="Link to section: High Contrast">#</a>High Contrast</h2>
<p>Both themes respond to the <code>prefers-contrast: more</code> media query for users who need stronger visual contrast between text, borders, and backgrounds. This is a browser or OS-level accessibility setting that requires no configuration on your part.</p>
<p>In light mode, high contrast overrides strengthen text and borders:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">High Contrast</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Property</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">minimal HC</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">clean HC</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--text</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--heading</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--border</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--code-border</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#000</code></td></tr>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--link</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#023b95</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#1a0a91</code></td></tr>

</tbody>
<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<p>In dark mode with high contrast, the overrides flip to maximum brightness:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="data tm-table" role="grid"><caption class="sr-only">High Contrast</caption>
<thead>
<tr role="row"><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">Property</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">minimal HC dark</th><th class="sortable" role="columnheader" aria-sort="none">clean HC dark</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--text</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#fff</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#fff</code></td></tr>

<tr role="row"><td role="gridcell"><code>--border</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#fff</code></td><td role="gridcell"><code>#fff</code></td></tr>

<tfoot></tfoot>
</table></div>
<p>To override high contrast values in <code>custom.css</code>, nest your rules in the matching media query:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#1572B6"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="7" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{;}</text></svg> css</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: css"><code class="language-css">@media (prefers-contrast: more) {
    :root {
        --link: #0000cc;
    }
}</code></pre></figure>
<h2 id="design-tool"><a class="heading-link" href="#design-tool" aria-label="Link to section: Design Tool">#</a>Design Tool</h2>
<p>The <code>demo/index.html</code> file is a standalone design tool for visually experimenting with theme settings without modifying any project files. Open it in a browser to see a full documentation page with an interactive settings panel that updates in real time.</p>
<p>Click the gear icon in the topbar to open the panel. It provides 16 knobs organized by category:</p>
<ul><li><strong>Layout</strong> -- sidebar position (left/right/hidden), sidebar width, TOC position (right/inline), content width</li><li><strong>Typography</strong> -- font kind (sans/serif/mono/system), font size, heading transform (none/uppercase/small-caps), heading separator (none/line/dots)</li><li><strong>Spacing</strong> -- density (compact/default/relaxed)</li><li><strong>Colors</strong> -- light/dark mode, accent color, topbar color, gradient strip (on/off)</li><li><strong>Components</strong> -- border radius, code block style (default/minimal/bordered), table style (default/striped/bordered)</li></ul>
<h3 id="exporting-settings"><a class="heading-link" href="#exporting-settings" aria-label="Link to section: Exporting settings">#</a>Exporting settings</h3>
<p>After adjusting the design knobs to your liking, click <strong>Copy CSS to clipboard</strong> to export your changes. The tool generates a <code>custom.css</code> snippet containing only the CSS custom properties you modified, ready to paste into your project's <code>docs/custom.css</code> file.</p>
<p>You can also click <strong>Copy link</strong> to get a URL that encodes all current settings, making it easy to share a design with collaborators.</p>
<h2 id="print-stylesheet"><a class="heading-link" href="#print-stylesheet" aria-label="Link to section: Print Stylesheet">#</a>Print Stylesheet</h2>
<p>Both themes include a comprehensive <code>@media print</code> block that produces clean, readable printed output suitable for PDF export. The layout switches to single-column with no max-width constraint, and all interactive and navigation elements are hidden when printing:</p>
<ul><li>Sidebar, table of contents, mobile TOC</li><li>Topbar and hamburger menu</li><li>Navigation links (previous/next), breadcrumbs</li><li>Search dialog and triggers</li><li>Copy/run buttons on code blocks</li><li>Theme toggle, feedback widget, edit links</li><li>Hero section, feature grid, reading progress bar</li><li>Site footer</li></ul>
<p>The layout switches to single-column with no max-width constraint. Colors reset to the light-mode palette for legibility on paper. Page breaks are avoided inside code blocks, tables, images, API entries, admonitions, and blockquotes.</p>
<p>To add custom print rules in <code>custom.css</code>:</p>
<figure class="tm-code"><figcaption class="tm-code-bar"><span class="tm-code-label"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#1572B6"/><text x="8" y="12" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="7" font-weight="700" fill="#fff">{;}</text></svg> css</span><span class="tm-code-actions"></span></figcaption><pre tabindex="0" aria-label="Code: css"><code class="language-css">@media print {
    :root {
        --text: #000;
    }
    .my-custom-element {
        display: none !important;
    }
}</code></pre></figure>

<script>(function(){var btn=document.querySelector('.theme-toggle');var states=['system','light','dark'];function getState(){var s=localStorage.getItem('selfdoc-theme');return(s==='light' || s==='dark')? s : 'system';}function apply(state){if(state==='light' || state==='dark'){document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',state);localStorage.setItem('selfdoc-theme',state);}else{document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-theme');localStorage.removeItem('selfdoc-theme');}btn.setAttribute('data-state',state);var labels={system: 'Theme: system. Click for light mode',light: 'Theme: light. Click for dark mode',dark: 'Theme: dark. Click for system theme'};btn.setAttribute('aria-label',labels[state]);}apply(getState());btn.addEventListener('click',function(){var cur=getState();var next=states[(states.indexOf(cur)+ 1)% states.length];apply(next);});})();(function(){var toggle=document.querySelector('.tm-hamburger');var sidebar=document.getElementById('tm-sidebar');var app=document.getElementById('tm-app');if(!toggle || !sidebar || !app)return;function openSidebar(){app.classList.add('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(focusable.length){focusable[0].focus();sidebar.addEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);}}function closeSidebar(){app.classList.remove('sidebar-open');toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');sidebar.removeEventListener('keydown',trapFocus);toggle.focus();}function trapFocus(e){if(e.key !=='Tab')return;var focusable=sidebar.querySelectorAll('a,button,input,[tabindex]');if(!focusable.length)return;var first=focusable[0];var last=focusable[focusable.length - 1];if(e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===first){e.preventDefault();last.focus();}else if(!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement===last){e.preventDefault();first.focus();}}toggle.addEventListener('click',function(){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}else{openSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape' && app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')){closeSidebar();}});document.addEventListener('click',function(e){if(app.classList.contains('sidebar-open')&&
 !sidebar.contains(e.target)&& !toggle.contains(e.target)){closeSidebar();}});sidebar.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(){closeSidebar();});});})();(function(){var groups=document.querySelectorAll('#tm-nav details.tm-tree-details');if(!groups.length)return;groups.forEach(function(d){var slug=d.querySelector('.tm-tree-label');if(!slug)return;var key='selfdoc-nav-' + slug.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-');var saved=localStorage.getItem(key);if(saved==='closed'){d.removeAttribute('open');}d.addEventListener('toggle',function(){localStorage.setItem(key,d.open ? 'open' : 'closed');});});})();(function(){function setup(container,scroller){if(scroller.scrollWidth <=scroller.clientWidth)return;container.classList.add('has-overflow');function check(){var max=scroller.scrollWidth - scroller.clientWidth;container.classList.toggle('scrolled-start',scroller.scrollLeft <=2);container.classList.toggle('scrolled-end',scroller.scrollLeft >=max - 2);if(container===scroller){container.style.setProperty('--scroll-x',scroller.scrollLeft + 'px');}}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',check,{passive: true});check();}function init(){document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(el){var pre=el.querySelector('pre');if(pre)setup(el,pre);});document.querySelectorAll('.table-wrap').forEach(function(el){setup(el,el);});}init();if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.has-overflow').forEach(function(el){el.classList.remove('has-overflow','scrolled-start','scrolled-end');});init();}).observe(document.documentElement);}})();(function(){var bar=document.getElementById('reading-progress');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!bar || !scroller)return;function update(){var height=scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.clientHeight;if(height <=0){bar.style.width='100%';return;}var progress=Math.min(scroller.scrollTop / height * 100,100);bar.style.width=progress + '%';}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',update,{passive: true});update();})();(function(){var COPY='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><rect x="8" y="8" width="12" height="12"/><path d="M4 16V4h12"/></svg>';var DONE='<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5"><path d="M4 12.5l5 5L20 6"/></svg>';document.querySelectorAll('.tm-code').forEach(function(figure){var code=figure.querySelector('pre code');var slot=figure.querySelector('.tm-code-actions');if(!code || !slot)return;var btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='copy-btn';btn.type='button';btn.setAttribute('aria-label','Copy code');btn.innerHTML=COPY;btn.addEventListener('click',function(){navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.textContent).then(function(){btn.classList.add('copied');btn.innerHTML=DONE;setTimeout(function(){btn.classList.remove('copied');btn.innerHTML=COPY;},2000);});});slot.appendChild(btn);});})();(function(){var tocLinks=document.querySelectorAll('.docs-toc-item');var scroller=document.getElementById('tm-content');if(!tocLinks.length || !scroller)return;var headings=[];tocLinks.forEach(function(link){var id=link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);var el=document.getElementById(id);if(el)headings.push({el: el,link: link});});var ticking=false;function update(){var top=scroller.getBoundingClientRect().top;var active=null;for(var i=0;i < headings.length;i++){if(headings[i].el.getBoundingClientRect().top - top <=100){active=headings[i];}}tocLinks.forEach(function(a){a.removeAttribute('aria-current');});if(active){active.link.setAttribute('aria-current','page');active.link.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest',behavior: 'smooth'});}ticking=false;}scroller.addEventListener('scroll',function(){if(!ticking){requestAnimationFrame(update);ticking=true;}},{passive: true});update();})();(function(){document.querySelectorAll('.heading-link').forEach(function(link){link.addEventListener('click',function(e){e.preventDefault();var url=window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + link.getAttribute('href');history.replaceState(null,'',link.getAttribute('href'));navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function(){var toast=document.createElement('span');toast.className='copy-toast';toast.textContent='Link copied!';link.parentElement.style.position='relative';link.parentElement.appendChild(toast);setTimeout(function(){toast.remove();},2000);});});});})();(function(){var article=document.querySelector('article');if(!article)return;article.querySelectorAll('table.tm-table').forEach(function(table){var thead=table.querySelector('thead');if(!thead)return;var ths=thead.querySelectorAll('th.sortable');ths.forEach(function(th,colIdx){th.addEventListener('click',function(){var tbody=table.querySelector('tbody');if(!tbody)return;var rows=Array.prototype.slice.call(tbody.querySelectorAll('tr'));var asc=th.getAttribute('aria-sort')!=='ascending';ths.forEach(function(h){h.setAttribute('aria-sort','none');});th.setAttribute('aria-sort',asc ? 'ascending' : 'descending');var allNum=rows.every(function(r){var c=r.children[colIdx];if(!c)return false;var t=c.textContent.trim();return t !=='' && !isNaN(t);});rows.sort(function(a,b){var ac=a.children[colIdx],bc=b.children[colIdx];if(!ac || !bc)return 0;var at=ac.textContent.trim(),bt=bc.textContent.trim();if(allNum)return asc ? at - bt : bt - at;return asc ? at.localeCompare(bt): bt.localeCompare(at);});rows.forEach(function(r){tbody.appendChild(r);});});});});})();requestAnimationFrame(function(){requestAnimationFrame(function(){document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior='';});});</script>

<script type="module">
import { openPalette, registerPaletteSource } from "../../js/palette.js";
let index = null;
async function search(query) {
  if (!query) return [];
  if (!index) {
    index = await import("../../pagefind/pagefind.js");
    await index.init();
  }
  const found = await index.search(query);
  const top = await Promise.all(
    found.results.slice(0, 8).map((r) => r.data())
  );
  return top.map((d) => {
    const excerpt = String(d.excerpt || "").replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "");
    return {
      label: d.meta && d.meta.title
        ? d.meta.title + " \u2014 " + excerpt
        : excerpt,
      hint: d.url,
      run: () => { window.location.href = d.url; },
    };
  });
}
registerPaletteSource(search);
function open() { openPalette(); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "k") {
    e.preventDefault();
    open();
  }
});
for (const t of document.querySelectorAll(
  ".search-trigger, .search-bar-trigger"
)) t.addEventListener("click", open);
</script>
